messages:
ryan: heads-up — after landing the kernel-router change last night we're seeing a p95 token latency regression on qwen-16b (~15%) for seq_len 512 workloads. Affected stack: fp8 kvcache + continuous-batching path.

maya: ugh. any repro traces? which kernel route did it pick instead?

ryan: repro script attached below (ran on dedicated staging). Router switched from k_calc_v2 -> k_calc_simd on longer prefixes. Profiling snippet: 
```
# perf logs (abridged)
seq=512 model=qwen-16b
router: selected k_calc_simd for layer 10..22
mean_latency_ms: before=7.2 after=8.3
p95_latency_ms: before=14.1 after=16.3
kvcache_mem_delta: +6% (fp8 path)
```

chen: interesting that mem increased — fp8 should reduce footprint. Could this be an alignment/prefetch mismatch with the simd kernels? I remember a corner with odd head_dim sizes.

sam: @ryan can you paste the model config? head_dim / kv dim details may trigger slow memcpy patterns.

ryan: model cfg: qwen-16b, heads=128, head_dim=64, kv_dim=8192 (per-shard layout). Router heuristic: prefers simd kernels when (seq_len>256 && batch<8) to reduce compute ops.

maya: batch-wise continuous batching heuristics changed last week. We started favoring smaller batches to reduce tail latency but that can increase memory churn for kv-prefetch. Could be interaction.

chen: hypothesis: simd kernel does extra unaligned loads for quantized KV (we store as fp8 packed bytes). When seq grows, prefetch windows overlap and eviction logic kicks in more often -> extra memcpy and decoding.

sam: can we reproduce switching kernel back to k_calc_v2? If p95 drops it's a regression in the router heuristics not the kernels.

ryan: quick A/B on staging: forced kernel=v2 -> p95 back to 14.2ms, mem delta -5% vs simd. So router decision is the immediate cause.

maya: good isolate. Next step: add a cost model adjustment that factors kvcache-precision impact. For fp8 path, penalize simd by +10% unless batch>=n.

chen: also let's try a micropatch in simd kernel: handle 64-byte alignment fast path for head_dim multiple of 64. I can prototype.

ryan: I'll open a perf job sweeping: seq in {128,256,512,1024}, batch in {1,2,4,8}, kernels={v2,simd}, kv_precision={fp16,fp8,bf16}. Collect p50/p95 and kv-eviction-count.

infra-bot: perf job queued: job_id=perf-20260318-001, nodes=4, expected ~2h. Link: https://perf.internal/jobs/perf-20260318-001

sam: also check Rope scaling param — qwen had a rot_scl tweak recently. RoPE scaling changes can change activation ranges and cause extra quantization error that forces more re-materialization. Could indirectly affect prefetch effectiveness.

maya: noted. Add ropescale in sweep grid. 

chen: quick note on eviction policy: current LRU-ish policy evicts entire prefix blocks when memory threshold hit. For fp8 we should try sub-block evictions (partial rows) to avoid full re-decode. That will reduce sudden spikes.

ryan: agreed. If we combine: router penalty + simd alignment fast-path + sub-block eviction we may recover tail. I'll coordinate canary.

maya: timeline? If infra-bot finishes perf job in ~2h we can review results and dogfood on staging for a day. If green, ship router tweak to canary.

sam: one more ask — log an additional field in traces: kvcache_evicted_bytes_per_request and kernel_name. Right now we only log total evictions per minute which is noisy.

ryan: will add. Also capturing raw memcpy counts from kernel would help (cc: @chen).

chen: trying the simd alignment patch now, will push a debug build to the perf job bucket.

maya: thanks all. If we see similar regressions in mixtral/mistral later, we should generalize the router cost model to include (model_family, head_dim_mod, kv_precision).

ryan: noted — I'll create an RFC after we have perf artifacts. For now, triage plan: 1) wait perf sweep 2) run simd alignment debug 3) add router fp8 penalty 4) experiment sub-block eviction.

sam: sounds good. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: perf job updated: simd-debug artifact uploaded -> https://perf.internal/artifacts/perf-20260318-001/simd-debug.tgz

ryan: uploading initial logs and the simple repro harness to the ticket: INF-1739. Ping me for access if you need it.

maya: ok let's regroup after 2h. Thanks!
